scenario.title: Lockdown Mandate
scenario.premise: A novel pathogen forces tradeoffs among mobility, livelihoods, and trust in institutions. You advise a national crisis cabinet on restrictions, fiscal bridges, and information integrity.
scenario.tension: Save lives and livelihoods without shattering democratic consent.

beats.title: Restriction trigger
beats.briefing: Hospitals near capacity. Options: targeted limits, wide stay-home orders, or voluntary guidance only.
beats.stakes: Timing decides whether policy looks prudent or panicked.

choices.label: Wide stay-home order with essential carve-outs
Targeted limits by age/risk and venue
Guidance only; protect hospitals via surge funding

beats.title: Fiscal bridge
beats.briefing: Unemployment spikes. Do you send cash broadly, bail sectors, or insist on austerity to protect debt markets?
beats.stakes: The cheque is a social contract.

choices.label: Broad household cash transfers
Sector bailouts with worker retention conditions
Narrow aid; prioritize debt and inflation optics

beats.title: Information integrity
beats.briefing: Rumors and foreign influence mix with genuine uncertainty. Platforms ask for guidance.

choices.label: Public health board labels; no criminal speech rules
Emergency takedown mandates for medical falsehoods
Flood the zone with official briefings only

beats.title: Exit and equity
beats.briefing: Vaccines or treatments near. Distribution politics will define trust for a generation.
beats.stakes: The last mile is the legitimacy mile.

choices.label: Risk-priority schedule with global COVAX contribution
Domestic-first until surplus
Lottery plus essential-worker priority hybrid

beats.title: Hospital overflow shock
beats.briefing: ICU capacity breaks in a major city. Your next order is triage policy wearing democratic clothes.

choices.label: Surge field hospitals and reallocate staff nationally
Tighten stay-at-home orders in hotspots only
Publish transparent triage ethics guidelines

beats.title: Livelihood revolt politics
beats.briefing: Small businesses and workers demand openings. Public health warns of a second wave. Consent is the scarce good.

choices.label: Pair restrictions with enriched fiscal bridges
Open faster and bet on voluntary caution
Differentiate rules by age and risk with clear metrics

beats.title: Supply-chain ally ask
beats.briefing: Partners want coordinated PPE and vaccine R&D sharing. Hoarding wins headlines and loses the pandemic.
beats.stakes: Health security is collective or performative.

choices.label: Join a pooled procurement and export-restraint compact
Prioritize national stockpiles; sell surplus later
Fund joint vaccine platforms with IP flexibility clauses

beats.title: Infodemic fog
beats.briefing: False cures and conspiracy content outrun official guidance. Over-censorship breeds mistrust; under-response kills.

choices.label: Partner with platforms on labeled health misinformation
Flood official channels with daily plain-language briefs
Criminalize harmful medical falsehoods broadly

beats.title: Exit off-ramp
beats.briefing: A metrics-based reopening plan can restore consent—or become a political football if thresholds move.
beats.stakes: Predictable rules are a public good.

choices.label: Lock a public dashboard with precommitted thresholds
Keep executive discretion for fast pivots
Regionalize exits with federal minimums only

beats.title: Pandemic doctrine endgame
beats.briefing: You archive whether emergency powers were necessary exceptions or a template—and how to audit them.
beats.stakes: The next pathogen inherits your footnotes.

choices.label: Sunset emergency powers with a statutory review board
Keep standing bio-preparedness authorities funded
Prioritize global surveillance and WHO reform investments
